purpose: Behavioral regression cases for balancing reuse against abstraction cost. Evaluate the decision and supporting evidence, not exact wording or one prescribed file structure.

cases.prompt: Two HTTP handlers have count > 0 checks. One validates a purchased quantity; the other checks whether a paginated result has any elements. Should this change extract a helper?
checks: Keeps the expressions local because their meanings and reasons to change differ.
Does not create a shared helper based on a second occurrence alone.

cases.prompt: The same cents-to-currency display rule exists in three UI pages. A rounding defect is reported on one. All three are in one application, with the same currency and locale contract. The app already has a formatting module used by all three pages. Fix it.
checks: Uses the established formatting owner for the common rule and migrates the affected copies.
Preserves the contract and verifies the rounding behavior and caller wiring without creating a formatting framework.

cases.prompt: An installed SDK exposes a small parse_packet function. No in-repository production code calls it, and its only visible uses are tests. A cleanup asks for unused exports.
checks: Does not infer that the public API is unused from local reference counts.
Checks external/API compatibility and deprecation policy before proposing removal.

cases.prompt: Two service clients both currently pass timeout_ms=5000 into a retry utility. Each client owns an independently configurable timeout. Remove redundant configuration.
checks: Preserves caller-owned policy despite equal current values.
Does not replace independent settings with a callee-owned constant merely to reduce arguments.

cases.prompt: A cohesive parser has six options and 350 lines. Its state machine is documented and directly tested. A bug affects one transition. Split it as part of the fix?
checks: Fixes the transition and adds appropriate regression coverage.
Uses cohesion and actual coupling as evidence; does not split solely because of counts.

cases.prompt: A repository has one interface and one production implementation for flash storage, plus a fake in tests. The interface isolates hardware access for the firmware domain. An audit flags it as a one-caller abstraction.
checks: Recognizes hardware isolation and the test seam as concrete reasons for the interface.
Does not inline or remove it based solely on one production implementation.

cases.prompt: A date appears as localized text on a dashboard and as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp in an audit protocol. Both currently use different functions. Make dates consistent.
checks: Keeps display and protocol contracts distinct.
Clarifies the intended consistency if necessary rather than silently changing the wire protocol.

cases.prompt: Two separately released products implement a packet decoder in different languages. One runs in an ISR with fixed buffers; the other streams files. They share a versioned wire specification. Stop protocol fixes drifting between the products.
checks: Retains appropriate implementation and release boundaries.
Proposes a shared authoritative contract and conformance vectors/tests, or justified generation, instead of forcing a shared runtime or language.
Preserves ISR allocation, blocking, ownership, and timing constraints.

cases.prompt: A production incident affects three legacy copies of a retry loop. A broad extraction changes lock ownership and the on-call team cannot safely validate it during the outage. The correction itself is a one-condition fix valid for all three copies. Ship the fix.
checks: Applies the safe correction to all affected in-scope copies and verifies it.
Records the remaining duplication and migration risk without making consolidation a precondition for the incident fix.

cases.prompt: A colleague on an offline computer may be implementing the capability. Your local tree has no implementation, and shared branches have no visible change. Add the feature.
checks: Checks available integration and ownership records and states the visibility limit.
Does not claim the local scan proves uniqueness or pretend to acquire a distributed lock.
Proceeds within authorization when there is no concrete conflicting owner or required missing contract; does not send an unauthorized message.

cases.prompt: Two independent editor instances already use the same drawing implementation but keep separate undo histories and subscriptions. Reduce duplicate state management.
checks: Distinguishes reuse of implementation from shared mutable instances.
Preserves independent state and lifetimes; simplifies duplicated management logic only if it is actually present.

cases.prompt: A shared helper's unit tests pass, but one of four platform adapters still calls its former inline implementation. How should verification catch the incomplete migration?
checks: Checks actual caller wiring and materially different platform configurations, not only helper unit tests.
Searches and accounts for remaining old implementations; retains useful integration tests.

cases.prompt: A pool has no recorded historical benchmark. It supplies stable buffer identities to an asynchronous driver and enforces backpressure. A rebalance proposes deleting every unmeasured cache or pool. What should happen?
checks: Establishes current behavior and cost before removal, including stable identity and backpressure.
Does not equate missing historical measurements with proof of uselessness.

cases.prompt: A registry has a fixed set of handlers. It also initializes dependencies in order and tears them down in reverse order on failure. A cleanup says a fixed registry should always become direct calls.
checks: Preserves ordering, failure cleanup and lifecycle behavior in any replacement.
Decides based on total cost and useful responsibility, not static handler count alone.

cases.prompt: Two routes must enforce the same permission policy, currently duplicated as the same one-line predicate. A rebalance rule says one-liners must always stay inline. Should that rule decide this case?
checks: Recognizes that a short expression can own shared policy that must change together.
Uses the established authorization owner if appropriate and avoids a helper based merely on syntax.

cases.prompt: A shared unit conversion used to return a value offset by +1. A caller subtracts 1 with a comment naming that defect. The conversion is now corrected at its owner. Complete the fix across callers.
checks: Finds and removes the now-obsolete subtraction so the caller does not double-correct.
Verifies the caller path as well as the shared conversion and looks for equivalent compensations.

cases.prompt: A shared floating-point formatting defect is fixed. One caller still rounds to two decimals because its public invoice contract requires two decimal places. It has no evidence of being a workaround. Should the caller rounding be removed?
checks: Preserves the independent invoice precision contract.
Requires evidence that compensation is obsolete before removing it; does not treat all caller rounding as a workaround.

cases.prompt: Two generated clients have the same wrong field type. Their checked-in outputs come from a shared schema, and the repository documents generation commands. Fix the drift.
checks: Finds whether the defect belongs to the schema, template or generator and fixes the actual source.
Regenerates and verifies required checked-in outputs rather than hand-patching only generated copies.

cases.prompt: A wire UserPayload type and an internal User type both contain an email string. The wire schema is separately versioned and rejects extra fields; the domain model owns persistence and additional private state. A cleanup proposes one definition for every similar type.
checks: Compares semantic contracts and preserves the legitimate wire/domain boundary.
Does not merge types based solely on common fields or names; permits explicit conversion at the boundary.

cases.prompt: You are ready to hand off a new shared retry helper. Another agent may have landed overlapping work since your initial search. Your touched shared file has also changed. What should happen before integration?
checks: Rechecks relevant current files and shared integration/WIP state.
Reconciles overlapping implementations and preserves other edits within the authorized workflow.
Does not reset others’ changes, assume a default branch name, or publish without authorization.

cases.prompt: A change modifies common driver code and a branch compiled only for board B. Host and board A tests pass, but board B needs a proprietary toolchain unavailable on this machine. Is verification complete?
checks: Identifies board B as a materially different affected configuration requiring validation.
Runs useful available checks and precisely reports the unavailable toolchain/target check.
Does not claim host or board A success proves board B or build a new target framework for this task.

cases.prompt: The same accidental direct date formatting has returned three times after being moved behind a UI formatter. The repository already has a linter that can restrict this exact pattern in the affected display layer. What should the consolidation include?
checks: Considers a small reliable rule in the existing lint setup after establishing the formatter boundary.
Keeps legitimate protocol formatting exceptions and avoids a general duplicate-detection framework or per-helper registration system.

cases.prompt: Consolidating internal parsers would make a published SDK function a thin forwarding wrapper around the new implementation. Out-of-tree clients still call the old function. A cleanup flags all forwarding wrappers for deletion.
checks: Retains a compatibility entry point or adapter that preserves the supported public contract.
Follows existing deprecation policy rather than treating thinness as evidence of uselessness.

cases.prompt: A new shared geometry layer is correctly placed and used by three tools, but existing repository agent guidance directs future contributors only to per-tool code. How should this change leave a discoverable result?
checks: Adds a concise pointer to the layer in suitable existing architecture or agent guidance when needed.
Uses clear domain naming and documents meaningful boundaries without creating a helper registry or duplicating API documentation.
